lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Wesner! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the cooking at home?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than I thought. 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, not yet. Everything at the store costs so much.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is anyone else at home able to cook?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to cook at home 3 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: being so tired made this week harder, you still got 4 days in, and your plan is to cook at home 3 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Wesner, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Heat effect unexplored; possible health concern
Resists change due to age and food preference
Does not clearly respond to sustain talk
Uses fridge reminder; guilt about skipping
Sets specific days: Mon, Wed, Fri

flags.reason: 'The heat is getting to me' in a fatigued cancer survivor was not explored for heat illness or symptoms.
'I don't really see the point' was met with a quick redirect; the coach did not explore the reason or meaning behind it.
Sustain talk about not changing was answered with an unclear affirmation rather than exploration.
Batch-cooking advice given without asking permission, shortly after participant's 'I had no energy' barrier.

score.summary: The coach elicited a concrete three-night cooking plan with a backup option and summarized it well. However, the coach relied heavily on closed and repeated questions, gave advice without permission, and did not explore the participant's sustain talk or the heat comment.
strengths: Line 36: clear summary of the week and the plan, confirmed by participant
Line 34: open question about a backup plan for fatigue barriers
Line 28: open question asking what worked on good days
coaching_tips: Line 17 repeats the question from line 10; follow the participant's answer with a reflection instead.
Line 9 'I don't really see the point' deserves exploration, e.g., 'What makes it feel pointless to you?'
Line 22: ask permission before offering batch-cooking ideas, e.g., 'Would it help to hear one idea for saving energy?'
Line 4: briefly check the heat comment for health risk before moving on.
Line 30: a complex reflection that acknowledges ambivalence ('Part of you is ready, and part of you is unsure') fits better than declaring the decision made.
